title: Short Read Assembly Using SPAdes
author: Frank O Aylward
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.v4se8we

steps.title: Download Raw Read Data
steps.instruction: Use the sra-toolkit to download raw sequencing read data in FASTQ format for the Staphylococcus phage (SRR6764339).

substeps.instruction: Verify the creation of SRR6764339_1.fastq and SRR6764339_2.fasta

steps.title: Configure SPAdes Environment
steps.instruction: Update the system PATH to enable the SPAdes program.

steps.title: Perform Initial Assembly with k=17
steps.instruction: Run the SPAdes assembler using a k-mer length of 17.

substeps.instruction: Execute: spades.py -1 SRR6764339_1.fastq -2 SRR6764339_2.fastq -o phage_17 -k 17 &> log.txt
Navigate to the output directory: cd phage_17
Review the assembled scaffolds in scaffolds.fasta using seqkit
Review the assembly log using: more log.txt

steps.title: Visualize Assembly Graph
steps.instruction: Install and use Bandage to visualize the de Bruijn graph from the assembly.

substeps.instruction: Launch the Bandage application via the File Explorer by double-clicking the Bandage file
In the GUI, go to File -> Load graph and select the assembly_graph.fastg file
Click Draw Graph in the left menu

steps.title: Perform Refined Assembly with k=117
steps.instruction: Re-run the assembly with a longer k-mer length to resolve knots and bubbles in the graph.

substeps.instruction: Exit the previous output directory: cd ..
Execute: spades.py -1 SRR6764339_1.fastq -2 SRR6764339_2.fastq -o phage_117 -k 117 &> log2.txt
Load the new FASTG file from the phage_117 folder into Bandage to visualize the improved assembly
Inspect the new scaffolds.fasta file to verify the sequence is in one large scaffold
